reference.source: Stiehm's Immune Deficiencies / Middleton's Allergy: Principles and Practice
clinicalPearls: An X-linked disorder of boys defined by an extreme and often fatal immune dysregulation triggered by Epstein-Barr virus infection
XLP1 results from SH2D1A mutation causing loss of the signalling adaptor SAP; XLP2 results from XIAP (BIRC4) mutation
The three classic manifestations of XLP1 are fulminant EBV-driven haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis, dysgammaglobulinaemia, and B-cell lymphoma
XIAP deficiency more often presents with recurrent haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis, splenomegaly and inflammatory-bowel-disease-like colitis, and lymphoma is uncommon
SAP is required for normal function of natural killer T cells and for cytotoxic control of EBV-infected B cells, explaining the catastrophic response to primary EBV
Any boy with fulminant or fatal infectious mononucleosis, or EBV-associated HLH, should prompt evaluation for XLP
Haematopoietic stem cell transplantation is the only curative therapy and is best undertaken before or after control of an HLH episode
reference.pathophysiology: X-linked lymphoproliferative disease is a genetic failure to regulate the immune response, classically unmasked by Epstein-Barr virus. In XLP1 the SH2D1A gene encodes the SLAM-associated protein SAP, an intracellular adaptor essential for signalling through the SLAM family of receptors on T cells and natural killer cells; its loss cripples cytotoxic killing of EBV-infected B cells and impairs natural killer T-cell development. In XLP2 the affected gene XIAP encodes an inhibitor-of-apoptosis protein important for inflammasome signalling and lymphocyte survival. In both, uncontrolled activation and expansion of T cells and macrophages during viral challenge drives a hyperinflammatory, cytokine-rich state that produces haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis, together with a spectrum of antibody deficiency and, in XLP1, lymphoma.
additionalDifferentials: Familial haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis from other genetic causes
Other primary EBV-susceptibility disorders (e.g. ITK, CD27, MAGT1 defects)
Common variable immunodeficiency presenting with dysgammaglobulinaemia
Very-early-onset inflammatory bowel disease (for the XIAP phenotype)
Severe primary infectious mononucleosis without underlying defect
additionalInvestigations: Flow cytometry for intracellular SAP and XIAP protein expression
Molecular genetic testing of SH2D1A and XIAP/BIRC4
Quantitative immunoglobulins and specific antibody responses
Natural killer and cytotoxic T-cell function assays
EBV viral load and HLH markers including ferritin and soluble interleukin-2 receptor
Enumeration of natural killer T cells (typically reduced or absent in XLP1)
redFlags: Fulminant or progressive infectious mononucleosis with cytopenias and organ dysfunction
Ferritin and inflammatory markers rising in keeping with evolving HLH
Recurrent HLH episodes or refractory colitis in a boy (XIAP phenotype)
reference.prognosis: The natural history is severe, with EBV-triggered HLH carrying high mortality, but early recognition, control of hyperinflammation, and haematopoietic stem cell transplantation markedly improve survival, particularly when transplantation is undertaken before the onset of fulminant disease.
pitfalls: Dismissing severe mononucleosis in a boy as an ordinary viral illness without considering XLP
Attributing hypogammaglobulinaemia to common variable immunodeficiency and missing an X-linked cause
Failing to test both SAP and XIAP, since their phenotypes overlap but differ in lymphoma risk
Delaying definitive transplant planning until after a life-threatening HLH episode
management: Immediate haemophagocytic-lymphohistiocytosis-directed immunochemotherapy, such as corticosteroids, etoposide and ciclosporin, to control fulminant hyperinflammation
Anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody rituximab to reduce EBV-infected B-cell burden and viral load
Immunoglobulin replacement for dysgammaglobulinaemia and antibody failure
Allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation as the definitive curative therapy, ideally before onset of fulminant disease
Surveillance for B-cell lymphoma in XLP1 and, in XIAP deficiency, management of inflammatory-bowel-disease-like colitis
Avoidance of live vaccines with careful monitoring of EBV viral load
Genetic counselling with SH2D1A and XIAP testing and screening of at-risk male relatives
